About Houston Expert Roofers

A free phone line and a set of plain-language roofing guides for greater Houston. It answers your call and connects you with an independent local roofer. It does not do roofing work.

Call (832) 662-4107 How the line works
  1. Home
  2. About

What Houston Expert Roofers is

Houston Expert Roofers is two things: a phone number that answers around the clock, and the roofing guides on this website. It is owned by Dominion Digital Group and operates as a d/b/a under that company.

The phone line answers with an automated assistant, finds out what is going on with your roof and where you live, and transfers the call to an independent, locally owned roofing company that takes work in that part of greater Houston. When that company is unable to answer, it receives your details so it can call you back. That is the whole service.

The name is the brand of the line, not a claim about any roofer's skill. The roofing companies are separate businesses. They inspect, price and do the work, and you pay them, not the line.

Why the site teaches you to check the roofer

Texas does not license roofing contractors, and every big Houston storm brings a wave of crews that leave when the claims run out. The line cannot vouch for anyone, so the guides give you the questions instead.

Plain answers

Each service page explains what usually goes wrong on Houston roofs and what a careful repair or replacement should include, so you can follow what the roofer tells you.

Local rules

Town pages cover permits, homeowner association approvals and the coastal windstorm program, which change from one city line to the next.

Sources you can read

Facts come from public sources such as the Texas Department of Insurance, city permit offices and the National Weather Service, listed at the bottom of each page.

How the line is paid

Calling is free for you, always. Roofing companies may pay the line a referral fee for calls it connects. That fee is the line's only income from roofing calls, and it never appears on anything you pay.

Because a company may pay for the referral, you should treat its estimate like any other: read it line by line, ask what each item means, and compare it with another quote if you want one. Nothing about the call obliges you to hire the company.

What you will not find here

No reviews, ratings, star counts, years in business, team photos, license numbers or promises about how fast someone will arrive. The line has none of those to offer honestly, so it does not claim them.

  1. Call the numberAn automated assistant answers (832) 662-4107 at any hour and asks which service you need, since the line also takes heating, cooling, pressure washing and water damage calls.
  2. Describe the roofA leak, missing shingles, hail, a limb on the roof or an old roof you want looked at, plus your part of greater Houston and how urgent it is.
  3. Get put throughYour call is transferred to an independent, locally owned roofing company, which hears a short summary before it picks up.
  4. Deal with the roofer directlyIt inspects, quotes and does the work, and you pay it (or your insurer does, as you arrange). If it misses the call, it gets your name, number, city and need to call you back.

Questions Houston homeowners ask

Who owns Houston Expert Roofers?

Dominion Digital Group owns it; Houston Expert Roofers is a d/b/a of that company. It operates both the phone line and the website, and it neither is a roofing contractor nor employs roofers.

Why does one number also answer air conditioning and water damage calls?

The same Houston line serves several home services: roofing, air conditioning and heating, pressure washing and water damage. That is why the automated assistant first asks which one you need, then routes a roofing call to a roofing company.

Are the roofing companies you connect me with vetted or certified?

The line makes no claim about any company's licensing, insurance, certifications, ratings or reviews, and Texas has no state roofing license to check. That is why the guides on this site explain what to ask for yourself: a certificate of insurance, a written contract, local references and permits where required. See how to check a roofer.

Is the information on this site legal or insurance advice?

No. It is general information gathered from public sources such as the Texas Department of Insurance, city permit offices and the National Weather Service, each listed on the page where it is used. Your insurance policy, your insurer and your city have the final word on your situation.

Roof trouble? Make one free call

Tell the automated assistant what the roof is doing and where you live. Your call is put through to an independent, locally owned roofing company in greater Houston, which looks at the roof and gives you its own price.
